layout_dets.text: In this book the authors try to bridge the gap between the treatments of matrix

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: theory and linear algebra to be found in current textbooks and the mastery of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these topics required to use and apply our subject matter in several important

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: areas of application, as well as in mathematics itself. At the same time we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: present a treatment that is as self-contained as is reasonably possible, beginning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with the most fundamental ideas and definitions. In order to accomplish this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: double purpose, the first few chapters include a complete treatment of material to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be found in standard courses on matrices and linear algebra. This part includes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: development of a computational algebraic development (in the spirit of the first

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: edition) and also development of the abstract methods of finite-dimensional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: linear spaces. Indeed, a balance is maintained through the book between the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two powerful techniques of matrix algebra and the theory of linear spaces and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The later chapters of the book are devoted to the development of material that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is widely useful in a great variety of applications. Much of this has become a part

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the language and methodology commonly used in modern science and en-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gineering. This material includes variational methods, perturbation theory,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generalized inverses, stability theory, and so on, and has innumerable applica-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions in engineering, physics, economics, and statistics, to mention a few.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Beginning in Chapter 4 a few areas of application are developed in some

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detail. First and foremost we refer to the solution of constant-coefficient systems

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of differential and difference equations. There are also careful developments of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the first steps in the theory of vibrating systems, Markov processes, and systems

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The book will be useful for readers in two broad categories. One consists of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: those interested in a thorough reference work on matrices and linear algebra for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: use in their scientific work, whether in diverse applications or in mathematics

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: itself. The other category consists of undergraduate or graduate students in a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: variety of possible programs where this subject matter is required. For example,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: foundations for courses offered in mathematics, computer science, or engineer-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing programs may be found here. We address the latter audience in more detail.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: algebra at the sophomore or a more senior level.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: material is most appropriately used as a second course in matrices or linear

layout_dets.text: There are many exercises and examples throughout the book. These range

layout_dets.text: In comparison with the 1969 edition of "The Theory of Matrices"by the first

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: author, this volume is more comprehensive. First, the treatment of material in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: first seven chapters (four chapters in the 1969 edition) is completely rewritten

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and includes a more thorough development of the theory of linear spaces and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transformations, as well as the theory of determinants.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: most applications is the subject of Chapter 12. It includes a complete description

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of commuting matrices. Chapter 13 is a thorough treatment of stability questions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
